clues: When you ask where he lives, he laughs it off — twice — and never answers.
His phone stays face-down; when it buzzes he angles his body so you cannot see the screen.
His flirt act cracks into a nervous laugh that sounds unrehearsed.
He flashes a tram ticket and a work badge — today's date, real laminate, his name on both.

stages.intro:
Someone in a striped shirt cuts across your path like he meant to.

"You look lost in a cute way," he says, smiling with too much practice. "Or maybe I just wanted an excuse."
stages.ask: He waits in your light, thumbs hooked in his pockets.

walk_away.result:
You give him a thin smile and keep walking.

"Your loss," he calls, soft enough to almost sound kind.

The square swallows him. You do not turn around.

stages.intro:
He matches your pace toward the fountain, close enough that his sleeve brushes yours.

"I'm not usually this forward," he says. "Tonight feels different. You feel different."
stages.ask: The water catches neon. He watches your mouth when you talk.

bail.result:
You step back into clearer air.

"Okay. Message received." He raises both hands, still smiling.

You leave before the smile can renegotiate.

stages.intro:
He stops under a dead streetlamp and tips his head toward the side streets.

"My place is close. Or we trade numbers and pretend we'll text. Your call."
stages.ask: The invitation hangs between you — warm, easy, a little sharp.

threat.text:
You follow him off the square.

The block turns quiet too fast. His hand finds your wrist — not romantic.

A door that was never his. Voices you did not agree to meet.

Unity Square keeps its lights on without you.

human.text:
His apartment is small, messy, real — dishes in the sink, a plant half-dead on the sill.

He makes tea he forgets to drink. You talk until the sky softens.

In the morning the square looks ordinary again. That feels like a gift.

threat.text:
You type the digits he dictates. The message you send later fails — number not in service.

At the hotel desk, a clerk mentions someone matching his description asking for your room.

You sleep with a chair under the handle.

human.text:
He saves your contact as "Fountain" and grins at his own joke.

A normal text arrives before midnight: made it home, hope you did too.

You answer. The night loosens its teeth.

decline.result:
"Not tonight," you say.

He nods once, almost respectful. "Worth a try."

You part at the metro mouth. The square feels wider on the walk back.
